Editor and PIE 39

editor_batch

Run several editor commands in order under one lease, one step per editor tick, with a fence after each (wait for shaders/asset loads/GC/async loading to settle; gc also collects garbage under an exclusive region/world lease). Returns {job_id} at once; follow it with batch_status. Steps may be wp_region_load {bounds:[minX,minY,maxX,maxY], name?} / wp_region_unload {name?}: the batch owns those World Partition regions and always releases them by the end. Other agents' queued interactive lease requests are served at fences. The batch keeps its own lease alive and runs to the end of its steps even if this server disconnects.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
lease_id string Optional The lease_id from lease_acquire this batch runs under. Optional only when this server holds exactly one lease.
lease string Optional Same as lease_id (kept for existing callers).
steps object[] Required
on_error "stop" | "unload_then_stop" Optional stop (default): halt at the failing step. unload_then_stop: halt, release loaded regions, then settle (idle, and gc if allowed) before reporting done. Regions are released in both cases.
idle_ticks integer Optional Consecutive idle ticks a fence needs (default 2).
fence_timeout_s number Optional A fence that never settles fails its step after this long (default 120).

editor_capture_viewport

Capture the active editor viewport and return it as an inline image block (plus a small text block with camera/width/height). Set HAYBA_CAPTURE_TO_FILE to also spill the image to a temp file path.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
width integer Optional
height integer Optional
wait_for_shaders boolean Optional If true, calls wait_for_shaders first (max_seconds=60, poll_seconds=1).

editor_cvar_get

Typed read of a console variable (int/float/bool) via KismetSystemLibrary getters. CAVEAT: UE's typed getters return type-defaults (0/0.0/False) for an unknown or mistyped cvar name, indistinguishable from a real zero value — this tool probes existence via the string getter when available and reports verified:false (plus a note) whenever the value cannot be confirmed real; treat verified:false as "do not trust this value". type defaults to float when omitted, with type_assumed:true in the response. NOT a freeform console runner — use editor_run_console_command for that.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
name string Required Console variable name, e.g. "r.ScreenPercentage"
type "int" | "float" | "bool" Optional Typed read: int | float | bool. If omitted, defaults to float and the response sets type_assumed:true.

editor_cvar_set

Typed set of a console variable, with a float read-back of the applied value. CAVEAT: the float readback returns 0.0 for a nonexistent cvar, indistinguishable from a real set-to-0 — this tool also probes the string getter (when available on this engine build) and returns ok:false + verified:false + a note when the readback proves the cvar does not exist (mistyped name). When no existence probe is available it stays ok:true with verified:false. Idempotent (retry-safe). NOT a freeform console runner — use editor_run_console_command for arbitrary commands.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
name string Required Console variable name, e.g. "r.ScreenPercentage"
value number | boolean | string Required New value (number, bool, or string)

editor_focus_actor

Frame an actor in the editor viewport by label — computes camera position from the actor's bounds and aims at its centre, entirely in C++. Roll is always 0 so the view never tilts. This is the correct 'framing tool'; do NOT hand-compute camera angles in python_run.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
actor_label string Required Label of the actor to frame in the viewport.
distance_scale number Optional How far back to sit, as a multiple of the actor's bounds radius (default 2.5; larger = further/more padding).
direction any[] Optional Optional [x,y,z] view direction (camera to actor). Default is a 3/4 front-right-above view. Need not be normalized.

editor_get_camera

Read the active editor viewport camera location + rotation. Net-new read counterpart to the legacy editor_set_camera. Rotation is [roll,pitch,yaw] degrees.

No parameters.

editor_get_output_log

Read the editor's output log, filtered by severity or regex and paged with since_line. The first thing to check when a command reported success but nothing happened — UE logs the real reason here.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
lines integer Optional
since_line integer Optional
severity_filter string Optional
regex_filter string Optional

editor_get_performance_stats

Editor frame timing: average fps, frame time, and the two thread times. These are whole-editor averages, not a profile of one operation — an idle editor with a compile running reads badly and that is not a scene problem. The thread times are cycle counters converted through FPlatformTime::ToMilliseconds; they were previously emitted RAW under _ms names, so every reading of those two fields used to be wrong by the platform cycle factor.

No parameters.

editor_get_state

One-shot consolidated native editor status: current map, who owns PIE (pie: none | user | agent:<owner>) and its phase, selected-actor count, Live Coding / shader / save activity, asset builds in progress, editor health, and the dirty (unsaved) package list (include_dirty:false skips that walk). The master gating probe before any action loop; after a pie_active refusal, poll it until pie is "none".

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
include_dirty boolean Optional Walk every loaded package for dirty_packages (default true). false skips the walk; the reply then has dirty_packages_skipped:"include_dirty".

editor_live_compile

Triggers a Live Coding compile of the running editor. It is asynchronous: poll the editor log for 'Live coding succeeded' or 'LogLiveCoding: Error', matching on a COUNT of terminal lines rather than presence, because earlier runs are still in the file. Compile ERRORS are not in the editor log at all — they are in UnrealBuildTool\Log.txt. A brand-new handler CLASS still needs a full editor restart; Live Coding cannot register one.

No parameters.

editor_pie_actor_inspect

INSPECT ONE LIVE PIE ACTOR without touching editor-world state: transform, bounds, tags, owner and a capped/paginated list of owned components with visibility, collision and component-space evidence. USE_WHEN: understanding a runtime road, controller, pawn or interaction target found by editor_pie_actor_list. Read-only.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
pie_instance integer Optional
actor_path string Optional Exact path returned by editor_pie_actor_list; safest and unambiguous.
actor_id string Optional Runtime object name; rejected if it matches more than one actor.
actor_label string Optional Editor label; rejected if it matches more than one actor.
component_filter string Optional Case-insensitive substring of component name or class.
component_offset integer Optional Default: 0.
component_limit integer Optional Default: 50.

editor_pie_actor_list

WHAT EXISTS IN THE RUNNING WORLD: paginated runtime actors from the selected PIE client/server, with exact path, class and transform. USE_WHEN: finding roads, controllers, interactable actors or spawned state while PIE runs. NOT_WHEN: querying the editor MainMenu world (actor_list). Use the returned actor_path for unambiguous follow-up calls.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
pie_instance integer Optional Select a PIE client/server from available_worlds. Omit for the sole or active world.
class_filter string Optional Case-insensitive substring of class name or class path.
name_filter string Optional Case-insensitive substring of runtime actor id or label.
tag string Optional Exact actor tag.
offset integer Optional Default: 0.
limit integer Optional Default: 50.

editor_pie_assert

Assert a UPROPERTY on a PIE actor holds a value. It is ONE OBSERVATION, not a wait: a command handler runs on the game thread, so it cannot advance the world, and a property it watches can never change while it blocks — an earlier version that pumped the ticker to fake waiting is what crashed the editor. So a false `matched` with `polling:true` means 'not yet', and the caller loops. Read observed_value_last before assuming the property is wrong; it is often the expectation that is.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
property_name string Required A UPROPERTY on the resolved actor, by reflection name
expected_value any Required Compared for equality. Numbers honour `tolerance`.
actor_label string Optional Editor label of the actor to inspect. Give this or actor_path.
actor_path string Optional Full object path in the PIE world
tolerance number Optional Float comparison slack — an exact match on a simulated float is rarely what you want
timeout_ms number Optional Accepted for signature compatibility. It does NOT make the call wait — see the note.

editor_pie_axis

Send analog input — gamepad sticks and triggers, mouse axes. Applies for the frame it is delivered, so send it again per step for sustained movement rather than expecting it to latch.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
key string Required Axis key name, e.g. "Gamepad_LeftX", "Gamepad_RightY", "MouseX".
value number Optional Axis value, normally -1..1. Applies for one frame.

editor_pie_capture_get

Read progress or the final whole-editor timing summary for a PIE capture. Reports aborted status if PIE stops or the selected world changes. If the editor becomes unsafe, the safety gate refuses this command, so an internal abort cannot be retrieved. GPU time, real WP cells, and NPC AI cost remain explicitly unknown.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
capture_id string Required

editor_pie_capture_start

Start a bounded asynchronous capture of observed editor ticker intervals, whole-editor thread timing, and process physical memory during an already-running PIE session. Returns a capture_id immediately; poll editor_pie_capture_get. Ticker intervals are a whole-editor proxy and the result gives no performance verdict.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
pie_instance integer Optional Required when more than one PIE world is running.
sample_frames integer Optional Default: 120.
warmup_frames integer Optional Default: 0.
actor_tag string Optional Optional exact actor tag to count in one capped scan at capture completion.

editor_pie_click_actor

CLICK AN EXACT LIVE PIE ACTOR WITHOUT OS INPUT. Reuses the world-projection safety seam, rejects Slate/UMG and Canvas HUD blockers, and repeatedly verifies the canonical local player and first Visibility hit. It dispatches the exact native primitive stage used by APlayerController only after its complete guard state is proven, avoiding InputKey's unchecked re-entrant trace window and all synthetic mouse routes. Hover fails closed because UE exposes no public route that preserves native hover state while guaranteeing zero OS cursor movement. Fails closed for ambiguous clients, absent/hidden/minimized viewports, offscreen/hidden/occluded actors, policy changes and active gestures. USE_WHEN: selecting a road, unit or world actor in background automation with a live visible PIE viewport. NOT_WHEN: hovering, truly headless/NullRHI PIE, or clicking UI controls (editor_pie_click_widget).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
pie_instance integer Optional Required when more than one PIE client owns a viewport.
actor_path string Optional Exact path returned by editor_pie_actor_list; safest and unambiguous.
actor_id string Optional
actor_label string Optional
component_name string Optional Require this owned primitive component to be the first Visibility hit.
sample "actor_location" | "component_location" | "bounds_origin" Optional Point to project before verifying the first Visibility hit. Defaults to bounds_origin; component_location requires component_name.
player_index integer Optional Local player ordinal inside the selected PIE world. Default: 0.
action "click" Optional Synchronously dispatches the exact guarded native primitive stage used by APlayerController. Hover is deliberately unsupported because UE exposes no public zero-OS-cursor route to its protected hover state. Default: "click".

editor_pie_click_widget

CLICK A CONTROL BY WHAT IT SAYS rather than by pixel. Finds the widget whose text, tag or type matches and clicks its centre, preferring an interactive one so matching a label presses the button containing it. Reports how many matched, so an ambiguous choice is visible instead of silent. USE_WHEN: pressing menu buttons. NOT_WHEN: you need an exact position.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
match string Required Text, tag or widget type to find on screen, e.g. "Start Game" or "SButton". Prefers an interactive widget, so matching a label presses the button containing it.

editor_pie_mouse

Drive the mouse in the running game: move, click, double_click, press, release, drag or scroll. press/release let you hold a button across calls; drag interpolates intermediate positions because widgets that track deltas ignore a single jump. x/y are ABSOLUTE desktop pixels — pass center_x/center_y from editor_pie_widget_tree straight through. Check focused_widget_after: if it says SViewport, the click missed the UI. PREFER editor_pie_click_widget when you know the label.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
action "move" | "click" | "double_click" | "press" | "release" | "drag" | "scroll" Optional press/release let you hold a button across several calls; drag does the whole gesture. Default: "click".
x number Optional Target X in ABSOLUTE desktop pixels — pass center_x from editor_pie_widget_tree unchanged. Required for everything except scroll, where it is optional and positions the cursor before the wheel.
y number Optional Target Y in ABSOLUTE desktop pixels — pass center_y from editor_pie_widget_tree unchanged. Required for everything except scroll, where it is optional and positions the cursor before the wheel.
to_x number Optional Drag destination X. Required for action:"drag".
to_y number Optional Drag destination Y. Required for action:"drag".
steps integer Optional Intermediate positions for action:"drag" (default 8, clamped 1..256). Slate quantises the pointer to whole pixels, so steps closer than a pixel apart are dropped rather than sent as no-op moves.
button "left" | "right" | "middle" Optional Default: "left".
delta number Optional Wheel notches for action:"scroll" (default 1). Positive scrolls up. Delivered as a real Slate FPointerEvent under the cursor, so it reaches ScrollBoxes, list views and combo boxes as well as the game.
coordinate_space "absolute" | "viewport" Optional How x/y are read. "absolute" (default) is desktop pixels, which is what editor_pie_widget_tree reports. "viewport" is relative to the top-left of the game window; only use it if you measured from the window rather than the tree. Default: "absolute".

editor_pie_press_key

Press a keyboard or gamepad button in the running game. pressed_and_released schedules the release on a later tick and RETURNS IMMEDIATELY — the key is still down when you read the result, which is what lets the game see the hold at all.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
key string Required Key name, e.g. "SpaceBar", "E", "Escape", "Gamepad_FaceButton_Bottom".
event "pressed" | "released" | "pressed_and_released" Optional pressed_and_released schedules the release on a later tick and returns immediately. Default: "pressed_and_released".
held_ms number Optional How long to hold before the scheduled release. The call does not block for this.

editor_pie_project_world

PROJECT A LIVE WORLD TARGET TO A VERIFIED CLICK CANDIDATE. Accepts an actor, owned scene component or [x,y,z]. absolute.available and x/y are present only when the point is on-screen, its PIE window is visible/not minimized, and Slate finds no UMG/modal obstruction. For actor/component clicks require target_click_ready:true too; it combines that Slate proof with the first world Visibility hit. USE_WHEN: diagnosing or clicking a road, unit or world-space target without OS input against a live visible PIE viewport.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
pie_instance integer Optional Select a PIE client from available_worlds when more than one owns a viewport.
actor_path string Optional
actor_id string Optional
actor_label string Optional
world_location [number, number, number] Optional
component_name string Optional Owned scene-component name/path. Requires an actor target.
sample "actor_location" | "component_location" | "bounds_origin" Optional Defaults to bounds_origin. component_location requires component_name; actor_location requires an actor without component_name.
player_index integer Optional Local player ordinal inside the selected PIE world. Default: 0.
trace_visibility boolean Optional Hit-test the Visibility channel at the projected point and report the first actor/component. Default: true.

editor_pie_screenshot

Capture the running game. Requests the shot and returns immediately; the engine writes the file a frame or two later, so poll with check_only:true and the same filename rather than assuming it is ready. NOT_WHEN: capturing the editor viewport outside PIE (editor_capture_viewport).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
filename string Optional Output path. An absolute path is used as-is; a RELATIVE name is anchored to the project screenshot directory (Saved/Screenshots/<Platform>) — it is NOT relative to the editor process, whose working directory is the Unreal install tree. Defaults to that directory with a timestamp. The response returns the RESOLVED ABSOLUTE path; poll check_only with that value. check_only:true REQUIRES this.
path string Optional Alias of filename. Accepted because the object_* tools call the same idea `path`; silently stripping it made check_only polls target a file that was never checked.
check_only boolean Optional Do not capture; just report whether the previously requested file (pass its filename!) has landed. The engine writes the image a frame or two after the request, so poll with this rather than assuming it is ready.
show_ui boolean Optional Include Slate/UMG in the capture. Defaults to true; set false only for a scene-only frame. Default: true.

editor_pie_set_text

Put a value straight into a text field and tell the game about it. PREFER THIS over editor_pie_type_text when you just need to get past a field — typed characters go wherever focus happens to be, can be eaten by a modal, and are lost if focus moves before the widget commits. Find the field by the text ON it (the placeholder counts, so an empty login box matches "Username"), or omit match to use the focused field. Returns readback+verified, so you know the value is actually in the box. USE_WHEN: filling a login/search/name field. NOT_WHEN: you are testing how the game itself handles keystrokes.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
text string Required The value to put in the field. Replaces what is there.
match string Optional Which field, by the text visible on it — the PLACEHOLDER counts, so an empty login box matches "Username". Omit to target whatever currently has keyboard focus.
commit boolean Optional Send Enter afterwards so the game's OnTextCommitted binding fires (default true). Most games read the value from that binding rather than polling the widget, so without it the box visibly contains the text and the game never receives it. Pass false for a multi-field form where Enter would submit early. Default: true.

editor_pie_sightlines

Observe collision sightlines in live PIE. Tests 1-32 explicit eye positions against one target point with one ECC_Visibility trace per sample (maximum 100 m each). Returns clear, blocked with first blocker, or unknown, plus clear/tested ratio. This is a collision sightline proxy, not rendered visibility, walkability, World Partition residency, or performance. Read-only; multiple live PIE worlds require pie_instance.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
pie_instance integer Optional Required when more than one PIE world is live.
eye_positions [number, number, number][] Required Explicit world-space eye positions in cm. Each must be more than 0 and at most 10000 cm from the target.
target_location [number, number, number] Required One explicit world-space target point in cm.

editor_pie_type_text

Type a string into the running game as character input, which is what text fields actually consume. Goes to whatever holds keyboard focus — click the field first. Read characters_accepted_by_ui, NOT characters_sent: the first says the text landed in a widget, the second only says it was sent. USE_WHEN: filling in a name or search box. NOT_WHEN: a single control key like Enter (editor_pie_press_key).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
text string Required Characters to send. They go to whatever holds keyboard focus, so click the field first.

editor_pie_wait_for

The polling half of a PIE wait: one observation of a property, with `polling:true` when the condition is not met yet, so the caller can loop until it is or until it gives up. It does NOT block for you — the handler occupies the game thread it would need to advance, which is the reason the previous blocking version had to be removed. Same shape as editor_pie_assert; use this name when you intend to loop and that one when you intend a single check.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
property_name string Required
expected_value any Required
actor_label string Optional Give this or actor_path
actor_path string Optional
tolerance number Optional
timeout_ms number Optional Accepted, but this call does not block — see the note

editor_pie_widget_tree

WHAT IS ON SCREEN RIGHT NOW in the running game: every visible Slate/UMG widget with its type, text and on-screen rectangle. USE_WHEN: before interacting — this is how you find a button instead of guessing coordinates. NOT_WHEN: inspecting a Widget Blueprint asset rather than the live screen (ui_query).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
filter string Optional Keep only widgets whose type, tag or visible text contains this. Omit for everything.
max_depth integer Optional How deep to walk the Slate tree. Default 40.

editor_run_console_command

Run an editor console command (stat unit, r.* toggles, LiveCoding.Compile, etc). Arbitrary console access, so it is gated by Plan Mode. Effects are reported by the console, not returned — check editor_get_output_log.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
command string Required

editor_save_all_and_quit

Save every unsaved package, then shut the editor down — in that order. Shutting down with a dirty asset parks the editor on a modal save prompt that nothing can answer, because the MCP port closes first; three editor deaths in one session each cost exactly the assets still unsaved. REFUSES to quit if anything is still dirty after the save pass, and names what is holding it up. Pass quit:false to save everything without shutting down. USE_WHEN: ending a session, or closing the editor to link C++. NOT_WHEN: you only want to save (asset_save).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
quit boolean Optional Set false to save and verify every dirty package without shutting down. Default: true.

editor_set_camera

Position the editor viewport camera for deterministic captures. To AIM it, prefer look_at:[x,y,z] (orientation computed for you, never tilts). Manual rotation is UE FRotator (pitch/yaw/roll), NOT xyz-euler. To simply frame an actor, use editor_focus_actor instead.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
location any[] Required World-space camera position [x, y, z] in cm.
look_at any[] Optional BEST way to aim the camera: a world point [x,y,z] to face. The orientation is computed in C++ (correct pitch+yaw, roll always 0 — the horizon never tilts). Use this instead of rotation whenever you know what you want the camera pointed at; you do NOT compute any angles yourself. Takes precedence over rotation.
rotation object (map) Optional Manual orientation (only if you are not using look_at). PREFERRED form: object {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees — unambiguous. yaw = heading (about the vertical/Z axis, the value you usually want); pitch = look up(+)/down(-); roll = horizon tilt and defaults to 0 (omit it — a non-zero roll is what makes the viewport 'look angled'). Array form is accepted as [pitch, yaw, roll] but its 3rd element (roll) is IGNORED so the camera never tilts by accident — do NOT pass [x,y,z] euler here, index 2 is roll, not yaw.

editor_set_viewport_mode

Switches the active editor viewport's view mode — wireframe to read geometry density, shader_complexity to find expensive materials, unlit to judge albedo without lighting. This changes what a HUMAN is looking at and does not change back on its own, so put it back to lit when you are done rather than leaving someone else's viewport in wireframe.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
mode string Required lit | unlit | wireframe | detail_lighting | lighting_only | shader_complexity

editor_start_pie

Start Play-In-Editor.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
single_step boolean Optional

editor_stop_pie

Stop the running Play-In-Editor session and return whether one was running. Call it before editor-only operations: many asset and level edits are unsafe or refused while PIE is live.

No parameters.

editor_stream_log

Tail recent UE log lines (paged via since_line).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
filter string Optional
since_line integer Optional

outliner_tree

Paginated world outliner: level actors with label, class, folder, and attachment parent — the agent's map of the level without dumping the whole world. Folder filters include descendants.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
folder string Optional Actors in this outliner folder and its descendants, e.g. "Buildings"
class_filter string Optional Exact class name filter, e.g. "StaticMeshActor"
name_filter string Optional Case-insensitive substring match on the actor label
limit integer Optional Max nodes returned (pagination) Default: 50.
offset integer Optional Pagination offset Default: 0.

render_camera

Render a camera view to disk and VERIFY the file landed (magic bytes + dimensions). Accepts either an actor reference or an inline transform. Calls wait_for_idle internally before capture.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
camera object Required
output_path string Optional Optional clean filename only (no path). Written without overwrite under Saved/Screenshots/Hayba; omit for a unique name.
width integer Optional Default: 1920.
height integer Optional Default: 1080.
format "png" | "jpg" Optional Default: "png".
wait_for_subsystems "shaders" | "assets" | "gc" | "pcg" | "world_tick"[] Optional Default: ["shaders","assets","world_tick"].
wait_timeout_s integer Optional Default: 30.
force boolean Optional render_camera is a known editor-crasher; it refuses unless force:true. Prefer set_level_viewport_camera_info + editor_capture_viewport (which now returns a real image block). Default: false.

selection_get

Full editor selection probe: selected level actors, content-browser assets, and selected components. Broader than actor_get_selection (adds assets + components) — the context probe for "apply to selection" tools.

No parameters.

wait_for_idle

Wait for UE subsystems (shaders/assets/gc/pcg/world_tick) to settle before reading back or rendering. Default = shaders+assets+gc+pcg.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
subsystems "shaders" | "assets" | "gc" | "pcg" | "world_tick"[] Optional Subsystems to wait on. Omit = shaders+assets+gc+pcg (world_tick excluded by default — it is always "busy" in-editor and yields false not-settled; request it explicitly only if you truly need a tick barrier).
timeout_s integer Optional Hard timeout in seconds. Default: 60.
pcg_actors string[] Optional Optional scope: only wait on these PCGComponent owners (full actor paths). Omit = all PCG actors in the active level.
world_ticks integer Optional When world_tick is in subsystems: wait at least N world ticks past request start. Default 1.

wait_for_shaders

Wait for UE shader compilation to settle (or timeout). Thin wrapper around wait_for_idle({subsystems:["shaders"]}).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
max_seconds integer Optional Upper bound in seconds (default 60).
poll_seconds number Optional Poll interval in seconds (default 1). NOTE: ignored — UE-side polling is fixed at 250ms.

Enhanced Input 3

input_add_mapping

Binds a key to an action inside a mapping context, optionally with modifiers and triggers. A modifier or trigger class name it cannot resolve is reported under unresolved_classes rather than silently skipped — so a reply listing fewer modifiers than you asked for is telling you something. Marks the context dirty; asset_save to keep it.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
mapping_path string Required Object path of an existing UInputMappingContext
action_path string Required Object path of an existing UInputAction
key_name string Required Engine key name, e.g. W, SpaceBar, Gamepad_LeftX. An unknown key is rejected.
modifiers any[] Optional UInputModifier class names, e.g. InputModifierNegate, InputModifierSwizzleAxis
triggers any[] Optional UInputTrigger class names, e.g. InputTriggerPressed, InputTriggerHold

input_create_action

Creates an Enhanced Input UInputAction — the 'what the player did' half of the system, independent of which key does it. Pick value_type by the shape of the input: Boolean for a press, Axis1D for a trigger, Axis2D for a stick. The asset is created dirty and unsaved; call asset_save to keep it. An existing name is an explicit error, because letting the engine ask would raise a modal dialog and hang every queued command.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
path string Required Package folder, e.g. /Game/Input
name string Required Asset name. A name already in use is refused rather than overwritten.
value_type string Required Boolean | Axis1D | Axis2D | Axis3D

input_create_mapping

Creates an empty UInputMappingContext — the 'which keys, in this situation' half of Enhanced Input. A context is what gets pushed and popped as the player moves between menus, driving and walking. Fill it with input_add_mapping. Created dirty and unsaved; asset_save to keep it.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
path string Required Package folder, e.g. /Game/Input
name string Required Asset name; an existing one is refused, not overwritten

Foliage 15

foliage_add_instance

Place one foliage instance at an exact transform. USE_WHEN: precise single placement. NOT_WHEN: covering an area — foliage_paint_at scatters at a density instead.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
foliage_type_path string Required FoliageType asset path, e.g. "/Game/Foliage/FT_Grass"
transform object Required Placement transform. `location` is required; the rest default.

foliage_add_instances

Bulk-add explicit world transforms for a foliage type via EditorFoliageLibrary.add_instances, chunked to avoid a game-thread freeze — the direct authoring verb (fixes the historic silent C++ add stub). NON-IDEMPOTENT (append). UNCERTAIN-API: errors clearly when add_instances is not python-exposed.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
foliage_type_path string Required Content path of the FoliageType asset
transforms object[] Required Explicit world transforms to place
chunk_size integer Optional Instances per add call (game-thread freeze guard) Default: 2000.

foliage_capability_probe

Report which UE Python foliage bindings are available (EditorFoliageLibrary + add/get/remove instances, procedural-foliage, HISM, FoliageType_InstancedStaticMesh) plus the engine version and whether a Landscape/StaticMesh collision surface exists — the graceful-degradation gate to call BEFORE any scatter/author op.

No parameters.

foliage_clear_type

Remove ALL instances of a foliage type from the level (destructive, one-undo, requires confirm:true). NON-IDEMPOTENT. UNCERTAIN-API: routes through EditorFoliageLibrary.remove_instances with a null box (all-instances) and errors clearly when unavailable.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
foliage_type_path string Required Content path of the FoliageType asset
confirm true Required Must be true — this removes ALL instances of the type (destructive)

foliage_get_instance_count

Return the number of placed instances of a foliage type across the level — the cheapest read to verify a scatter/add/remove landed. UNCERTAIN-API: degrades to null + a warning when instance introspection is not python-exposed.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
foliage_type_path string Required Content path of the FoliageType asset

foliage_list_types

List the FoliageType assets in use in the current level, with instance counts. USE_WHEN: before adding or removing foliage, to learn what is already there.

No parameters.

foliage_paint_at

Scatter foliage over a circular area at a density, as the foliage paint brush does. USE_WHEN: dressing terrain. NOT_WHEN: you need one instance at an exact spot.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
foliage_type_path string Required FoliageType asset path to scatter
location object Required World-space centre of the painted area
radius number Optional Brush radius in cm; defaults to 200
density integer Optional Maximum number of placement attempts; defaults to 5
seed integer Optional Deterministic scatter seed; defaults to 1337

foliage_remove_in_bounds

Remove instances of a foliage type inside an axis-aligned box (center + half-extent) and return the delta count. NON-IDEMPOTENT (delete). UNCERTAIN-API: EditorFoliageLibrary.remove_instances signature/box arg is probed and errors clearly when unavailable.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
foliage_type_path string Required Content path of the FoliageType asset
center number[] Required [x,y,z] world center of the removal box
extent number[] Required [x,y,z] half-extent of the removal box

foliage_remove_instances

Remove foliage instances of a type inside a world-space box. Returns how many were removed, so an unexpected zero is visible rather than silent.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
foliage_type_path string Required FoliageType whose instances to remove
bounds object Required World-space box; instances inside it are removed.

foliage_replace_mesh

Swap the StaticMesh bound to a FoliageType (bulk re-theming — every existing instance re-renders with the new mesh) and read the binding back. Set-to-value (retry-safe).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
foliage_type_path string Required Content path of the FoliageType asset to re-mesh
new_mesh_path string Required Content path of the StaticMesh to bind, e.g. "/Game/Meshes/SM_Rock"

foliage_scan_types

Enumerate the foliage types used in the level (across all InstancedFoliageActors) with mesh path, density, radius and instance count. Paginated. The read entry point so agents stop guessing foliage type asset paths. UNCERTAIN-API: type enumeration is probed and degrades to [] + a warning.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
limit integer Optional Max foliage types returned (pagination) Default: 50.
offset integer Optional Pagination offset Default: 0.

foliage_scatter_paint

Deterministic area scatter: ground-trace downward onto landscape/collision inside a circular radius at a target density, with per-instance yaw + uniform-scale jitter and optional align-to-normal, then commit via add_instances. Refuses before UE transport above 10000 candidates; reduce radius/density or split into non-overlapping regions. Same seed to same placement. NON-IDEMPOTENT (append). This is the low-level authoring verb, NOT the PLUMB-validated world_generate flagship. UNCERTAIN-API: needs a collision surface (see foliage_capability_probe.surface_actors) and add_instances exposure.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
foliage_type_path string Required Content path of the FoliageType asset
center custom[] Required [x,y,z] finite world center of the scatter region
radius custom Required Scatter radius in world units (max 100000)
density_per_100m2 custom Required Target instances per 100x100 unit cell (max 10000)
seed custom Optional Deterministic signed 32-bit RNG seed Default: 1337.
scale_min custom Optional Per-instance uniform scale minimum (max 100) Default: 1.
scale_max custom Optional Per-instance uniform scale maximum (max 100) Default: 1.
align_normal boolean Optional Align instances to the ground-hit normal Default: false.
trace_height custom Optional Downward trace half-height (max 1000000) Default: 100000.

foliage_type_create

Create (or reuse if present) a FoliageType_InstancedStaticMesh asset from a StaticMesh with optional initial density — the entry point for all foliage authoring. Reuses an existing asset at the path (retry-safe read-back) but is classified NON-IDEMPOTENT as an asset-create lifecycle op. UNCERTAIN-API: FoliageType factory/class is probed and errors clearly when not python-exposed.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
static_mesh_path string Required Content path of the source StaticMesh, e.g. "/Game/Meshes/SM_Tree"
dest_path string Required Destination folder for the new FoliageType asset, e.g. "/Game/Foliage"
name string Required Asset name for the new FoliageType, e.g. "FT_Tree"
density number Optional Optional initial density

foliage_type_inspect

Read every authored param of a single FoliageType (density, radius, scale X/Y/Z intervals, z-offset, align-to-normal, random-yaw, collision, cast-shadow, cull distance) plus mesh path and instance count — the paired read for verify/diff before a foliage_type_set_params write.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
foliage_type_path string Required Content path of the FoliageType asset, e.g. "/Game/Foliage/FT_Grass"

foliage_type_set_params

Set the core authoring knobs on a FoliageType — density, radius, scale range (X/Y/Z), align-to-normal, random-yaw, world collision, cast-shadow, and cull start/end — then save + read back which keys changed. Set-to-value (retry-safe); omitted fields untouched. UNCERTAIN-API: unknown property spellings land in unchanged_keys[] rather than being silently lost. Returns ok:false (with warnings[]) when NONE of the requested params applied.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
foliage_type_path string Required Content path of the FoliageType asset to edit

Gameplay Ability System 4

gas_apply_effect

Needs the optional HaybaMCPGAS plugin in your project.

Applies a gameplay effect to an actor's ability system component, for checking that an effect does what you think before wiring it into gameplay. Refuses an actor without an ability system component by name. An Instant effect changes attributes and leaves no active handle behind, so an empty handle is not a failure.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription

effect_path string Required
level number Optional

gas_create_ability

Needs the optional HaybaMCPGAS plugin in your project.

Creates a UGameplayAbility blueprint. Lives in the optional HaybaMCPGAS satellite plugin, which auto-disables when the engine's GameplayAbilities plugin is off — so an Unknown command here means the satellite is not installed in this project, not that the command is missing. The ability is created empty; grant it to an actor with gas_grant_ability.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
path string Required Package FOLDER. Note this differs from blueprint_create / material_create / metasound_create, whose package_path is the full asset path with its last component discarded.
name string Required

gas_create_effect

Needs the optional HaybaMCPGAS plugin in your project.

Creates a UGameplayEffect blueprint — the data asset that changes attributes, the unit GAS actually applies. duration_policy decides whether it fires once (Instant), ticks for a while (HasDuration) or persists until removed (Infinite). Part of the optional HaybaMCPGAS satellite.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
path string Required Package folder
name string Required
duration_policy string Optional Instant | HasDuration | Infinite
duration_seconds number Optional Only meaningful with HasDuration
modifiers any[] Optional Attribute modifiers: attribute, op, magnitude

gas_grant_ability

Needs the optional HaybaMCPGAS plugin in your project.

Grants an ability to an actor's ability system component. It refuses an actor with no UAbilitySystemComponent rather than silently doing nothing, and refuses an uncompiled ability blueprint (no class default object) — both verified live. Grants made in the editor world are editor state, not gameplay state.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
actor_path string Required Must own a UAbilitySystemComponent — a plain actor is refused by name
ability_path string Required Object path of a UGameplayAbility blueprint
level number Optional
input_id number Optional

Leases and batches 6

batch_status

Progress or result of an editor_batch job: status running|succeeded|failed, phase, the step it is on, what a fence is waiting for, per-step results, loaded regions, yields to other agents. wait_s polls until done.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
job_id string Required
wait_s number Optional Poll until the batch is done or this many seconds pass (default 0: answer now).

lease_acquire

Reserve part of the editor (world, World Partition region, asset, actor, PIE, or everything) so other agents do not change it mid-sequence. Never blocks: returns {status:"granted", lease_id} or {status:"queued", ticket, position, holder_owner, eta_s, poll_after_s}; poll by calling again with ticket. Granted leases are renewed automatically until lease_release.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
resources string | object[] Optional What to lock. Required unless ticket is given.
mode "shared" | "exclusive" Optional Default exclusive. Shared lets other readers hold the same resource.
ttl_s number Optional Lease lifetime in seconds (default 120, max 900). Renewed automatically while this server runs.
lane "interactive" | "long" Optional interactive (default) is served first; long is for bulk work and ages to the front after a while.
ticket string Optional The ticket from an earlier queued answer, to poll for the grant.
label string Optional What the lease is for, shown to other agents in lease_status.
bind_connection boolean Optional Default true: a disconnect orphans the lease for up to 60 seconds, unless it expires sooner or its owner renews it.

lease_adopt

Make this connection act as the owner of a live lease: later commands that name no owner run as that owner, and the owner's orphaned connection-bound leases re-bind here. Needs lease_id and its owner. Connection adoption ends on close; repeat after reconnect. A confirmed adoption also switches this server's process-wide envelope owner and manual lease_id, which remain set across reconnects and unknown-id replies until explicitly changed. It does not start auto-renew or transfer existing renewal timers; renew or release the adopted lease yourself.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
owner string Required The owner of the lease (HAYBA_AGENT_ID).
lease_id string Required A live lease of that owner.

lease_release

Release a lease (lease_id), withdraw a queued ticket (ticket), or release everything you hold (all:true). Send exactly one. Other agents waiting on it can then be granted.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
lease_id string Optional A lease you hold (the lease_id lease_acquire returned).
token string Optional Deprecated alias of lease_id; send lease_id.
ticket string Optional A queued request to withdraw (the ticket lease_acquire returned).
all true Optional Release every lease and withdraw every ticket you hold.

lease_renew

Extend leases you hold. With lease_id, that lease; with nothing, every lease you hold, which also revives leases the editor orphaned when this server's connection dropped. Rarely needed: leases granted by lease_acquire are renewed in the background.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
lease_id string Optional The lease_id lease_acquire returned (ls_...). Omit it to renew every lease you hold.
token string Optional Deprecated alias of lease_id; send lease_id.
ttl_s number Optional New lifetime from now, in seconds (max 900). Omitted: each lease keeps its own TTL.

lease_status

Who holds or waits for which editor resources, the enforcement mode (off / advisory / enforced_for_writes / enforced), the identified agents the editor sees as connected (active_owners), and which of your leases this server is renewing.

No parameters.

level_create

Create a new empty level asset. Does not open it — follow with level_load to switch the editor to it.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription

path string Optional

Name and actor count of the level currently open. The cheapest way to confirm which level you are actually editing before making changes.

No parameters.

level_goto_bookmark

Moves the editor viewport to a stored bookmark. This changes what a human is looking at, so it is not a neutral read — prefer editor_set_camera when you just need a viewpoint for a capture. NOT VERIFIED LIVE: described from the handler source.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
name string Required A bookmark previously stored by level_set_bookmark

level_list

List every level asset in the project. Use it to find the exact path level_load wants.

No parameters.

level_load

Open a level in the editor, replacing the current one. UNSAVED CHANGES IN THE CURRENT LEVEL ARE AT RISK — call level_save first.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
path string Required

level_save

Save the current level. Optional path is an expected current-level package guard, not Save As; a mismatch is refused before mutation. A map or external actor package requiring a save, including clean packages requiring transient-reference repair, is refused before mutation when its file is read-only (code package_read_only, data.make_writable_hint). Saving runs unattended and cannot open a modal dialog. Returns saved, path, dirty and verified readback for that package only, not external actor packages. Plan Mode gated; disk persistence is not undoable.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
path string Optional

level_set_bookmark

Stores a named camera position in the current level so it can be returned to later. Bookmarks live in the LEVEL, so this dirties the map and persists only if the level is saved — do not use it as scratch state on a map someone else is working in. NOT VERIFIED LIVE: described from the handler source, because verifying it means dirtying a real level.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
name string Required Bookmark identifier
location any[] Optional [x,y,z]; defaults to the current viewport camera position when omitted
rotation any[] Optional [pitch,yaw,roll]

wp_get_cells

A spatial summary of where actors are: it bins every actor in the editor world onto a fixed 512m grid and reports per-bin counts and the classes that dominate each. These are NOT the World Partition runtime cells — cell ids and bounds will not match the partition's own, which is why the reply says cell_source. Requires World Partition to be enabled on the map; use it to find the busy regions before deciding where to look.

No parameters.

wp_get_streaming_state

Answers one question honestly: does the current editor world use World Partition. It previously also reported a hard-coded source_count of 0 — a field named for a measurement that always answers zero reads as "measured, none found", so it now names itself not_enumerated instead of inventing a number.

No parameters.

material_connect_nodes

Connect two nodes in a material graph or connect a node output to a material property. IMPORTANT for multi-output sources (esp. MaterialFunctionCall): you MUST pick the output pin with from_output (the pin NAME) or from_output_index — otherwise the call is rejected, because defaulting to the first output silently swaps function outputs (e.g. Albedo and F0). Get the real pin names/order from material_get_info.expressions[].outputs[]. May return clutter-prevention suggestions: use named reroutes when a source fans out to 2+ targets, or a reroute knee node when a wire would run backward/over another node.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
material_path string Optional Path to the material asset (either this or function_path required)
function_path string Optional Path to the material function asset (either this or material_path required)
from_node string Required ID or name of the source node
from_output string Optional Output pin NAME on the source node (from material_get_info.expressions[].outputs[].name). REQUIRED when the source has >1 output (e.g. a material function) unless you pass from_output_index.
to_node string Optional ID or name of the target node
to_input string Optional Input pin name on the target node
to_input_index integer Optional Target input pin by index (unnamed pins, e.g. Substrate slab inputs)
from_output_index integer Optional Source output pin by index (default 0)
to_property string Optional Target material output, e.g. base_color, normal, front_material (Substrate), displacement (Nanite tessellation - needs material_set_property enable_tessellation=true)

material_get_info

Inspect a material, material function, or material instance: properties, parameters, and the full expression graph. Parameter expressions expose their authored parameter_name, parameter_type, typed default_value, and explicit metadata/default availability. For materials, material_outputs[] distinguishes stored property wires from compiler-active terminals (important when Use Material Attributes retains ignored legacy wires). Each expression input includes its source edge (from_node + from_output), each node reports output_consumed + reachable_from_output, and dead_nodes[] lists every node NOT reachable from a compiler-active material output — i.e. provably dead, safe to delete (no delete-recompile-compare needed).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
path string Required Path to the material or material instance to inspect

material_set_property

Stage strict master-material settings with observed readback. Set used_with_spline_meshes:true for spline routes, then call material_compile to compile the required permutation and save.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
material_path string Required Path to the master material asset
properties object Required Material settings. Allowlisted boolean used_with_* flags are staged with verified readback; use used_with_spline_meshes:true for UE spline routes, then call material_compile to compile and save.

material_validate

Statically check a material OR material FUNCTION graph for translator-crash-prone wiring WITHOUT compiling: reroutes/named-reroutes used downstream that resolve to no input, and connections to non-existent output indices — both trigger an uncatchable HLSL-translator assert that kills the editor. material_compile runs these same checks and refuses to compile when any fail, so call this first to fix issues safely.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
material_path string Optional Path to the master material to validate (either this or function_path)
function_path string Optional Path to a material FUNCTION to validate (either this or material_path)

metasound_add_node

Needs the optional HaybaMCPMetaSound plugin in your project.

Needs the optional HaybaMCPMetaSound plugin in your project.

Conforms the asset to its document, initializes editor node locations, validates, and saves explicitly. Half-authored graphs are never implicitly saved by node edits. With save true, a read-only package is refused before conforming (code package_read_only, data.make_writable_hint). A save that fails after conforming returns ok:false, valid:true, mutation_status applied_unsaved.

Networking 2

net_debug

Toggles the networking stat overlay (stat net) and packet-handler log stats in the editor viewport. Reach for it when diagnosing replication during PIE. It is a viewport overlay, so the effect is visible in a screenshot rather than in this reply; the reply only tells you the console commands were issued.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
enabled boolean Required true turns the net stat overlay and packet-handler logging on, false turns both off
channels any[] Optional Reported back as channels_applied. Defaults to ["all"]. Currently descriptive only — the same overlay is enabled whatever you pass.

net_set_replication

Sets replication flags on one actor in the editor world and marks its level dirty — this edits the LEVEL, so the change persists only if the level is saved, and it is not something to try on a map someone is working in. Every parameter is validated before anything is written, so a rejected request leaves the actor untouched.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
actor_path string Required Actor name, label, or full object path in the current editor world
replicate boolean Required Whether the actor replicates at all
always_relevant boolean Optional Left alone when omitted, rather than reset to false
net_dormancy string Optional Awake | Initial | DormantAll. DORM_Never and DORM_DormantPartial cannot be expressed — an unrecognised value is rejected and nothing is written.
replicated_components any[] Optional Component names to mark replicated. Ones that do not resolve come back under missing_components rather than being dropped.

Niagara 14

niagara_activate

Activate (optionally reset) or deactivate a live NiagaraComponent to (re)start/stop the effect — needed because many template systems ship auto_activate=false. SET-SUCCESS: applied:true only when the activate/deactivate call ran; reports the resulting active flag. Idempotent set-to-state.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
component string Required NiagaraComponent object path OR an actor label/path carrying one
reset boolean Optional Reset the simulation when (re)activating Default: true.
deactivate boolean Optional Deactivate instead of activate Default: false.

niagara_advance_simulation

Deterministically tick a live NiagaraComponent's sim by N seconds at a fixed dt (AdvanceSimulation) so a screenshot is reproducible — the deterministic-preview primitive the vision loop needs (a transient effect is invisible at t=0). Refuses before UE transport above 7200 native ticks; increase tick_dt or advance in bounded chunks. SET-SUCCESS: applied:true only when the advance call ran; arg order probed defensively. NON-IDEMPOTENT: each call advances the sim cumulatively, so a repeat/retry compounds simulated time — re-run from a fresh spawn for a reproducible frame.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
component string Required NiagaraComponent object path OR an actor label/path carrying one
seconds custom Required How many seconds of simulation to advance (max 60)
tick_dt custom Optional Fixed per-tick delta seconds (0.004166666666666667..1) Default: 0.0167.

niagara_capability_probe

Probe whether the Niagara plugin and its python surface are available (NiagaraSystem/Component/FunctionLibrary classes, spawn entry points, and which set_variable_* setters exist). The cheap capability gate to call before any other niagara tool so an agent knows what will work in this editor build.

No parameters.

niagara_component_inspect

Read a live NiagaraComponent's runtime state: active/paused flags and the system asset it plays — the read-back/verify tool for runtime control ops (pairs with niagara_activate / niagara_param_set).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
component string Required NiagaraComponent object path OR an actor label/path carrying one

niagara_create_from_template

The HONEST authoring path: duplicate an existing template NiagaraSystem to a new content path and rename it. Since UE Python cannot build emitter graphs, template-instantiation is the supported creation verb (flagged with the engine-limit note). Non-idempotent (creates an asset); idempotent-by-path (returns created:false if the target exists).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
template_path string Required Content path of an existing NiagaraSystem to duplicate
dest_path string Required Destination content folder, e.g. "/Game/VFX"
name string Required Asset name for the new system
dry_run boolean Optional Preview the target path without duplicating Default: false.

niagara_list_components

Enumerate Niagara components on placed actors in the editor world (system path + active flag), optionally filtered by system substring or active-only, paginated — the "what VFX is currently in the scene" read tool.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
system_filter string Optional Only return components whose system path contains this substring
active_only boolean Optional Only return currently-active components Default: false.
limit integer Optional Max components to return Default: 50.
offset integer Optional Offset for pagination Default: 0.

niagara_param_list

List just the exposed USER parameters of a NiagaraSystem asset (name/type/is_data_interface) — the contract an agent needs before niagara_param_set. Cheaper focused variant of niagara_system_inspect. Exposed-parameter enumeration is UNCERTAIN-API; unresolved reflection is surfaced in warnings[].

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
system_path string Required Content path of the NiagaraSystem asset

niagara_param_set

Set one USER variable on a live NiagaraComponent (float/int/bool/vec2/vec3/vec4/quat/color/position/object) and mark render state dirty. Named niagara_param_set to avoid colliding with the dormant satellite-plugin C++ niagara_set_param command; broadens value_type coverage. SET-SUCCESS: UE setters return void, so applied:true is reported ONLY when a setter probe ran without raising — otherwise ok:false + applied:false + a warning (never ok:true with an unapplied change).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
component string Required NiagaraComponent object path OR an actor label/path carrying one
param_name string Required User parameter name (with or without the "User." prefix)
value_type "float" | "int" | "bool" | "vec2" | "vec3" | "vec4" | "quat" | "color" | "position" | "object" Required Value type of the parameter
value any Required The value: number (float/int), bool, [x,y,z] arrays for vectors/color, or an object path string

niagara_place_actor

Place a PERSISTENT NiagaraActor in the level (survives save, undoable, selectable) with a system assigned — for level-dressing VFX an author wants to keep and re-edit, vs the transient niagara_spawn_transient. Non-idempotent. Surfaces asset_assigned as a set-success flag (ok:false if the system asset could not be assigned).

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
system_path string Required Content path of the NiagaraSystem
location number[] Optional World location [x,y,z] Default: [0,0,0].
rotation number[] Optional Rotation [roll,pitch,yaw] degrees Default: [0,0,0].
scale number[] Optional Scale [x,y,z] Default: [1,1,1].
label string Optional Optional actor label for the placed NiagaraActor
dry_run boolean Optional Resolve the system without placing an actor Default: false.

niagara_set_user_param_default

Set the DEFAULT value of an exposed user parameter ON the system asset (persists to the saved asset), not just a live component — the param-pack vehicle for customizing instantiated templates. SET-SUCCESS: applied:true only when a setter ran on the exposed-parameter store; the store is UNCERTAIN-API so failures surface ok:false + applied:false + warnings, never a silent no-op. Optionally saves the asset.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
system_path string Required Content path of the NiagaraSystem asset
param_name string Required Exposed user parameter name
value_type "float" | "int" | "bool" | "vec2" | "vec3" | "vec4" | "quat" | "color" | "position" | "object" Required Value type of the parameter
value any Required The default value (same encoding as niagara_param_set)
save boolean Optional Save the asset after setting the default Default: false.

niagara_spawn_transient

Spawn a TRANSIENT (auto-destroy) Niagara system at a world location/rotation/scale — the workhorse placement verb for one-shot VFX. Non-idempotent (each call spawns a new component). Named niagara_spawn_transient to avoid colliding with the dormant satellite-plugin C++ niagara_spawn command; adds scale, auto_activate and dry_run. For a persistent, savable effect use niagara_place_actor.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
system_path string Required Content path of the NiagaraSystem to spawn
location number[] Optional World location [x,y,z] Default: [0,0,0].
rotation number[] Optional Rotation [roll,pitch,yaw] degrees Default: [0,0,0].
scale number[] Optional Scale [x,y,z] Default: [1,1,1].
auto_destroy boolean Optional Auto-destroy the component when the effect completes Default: true.
auto_activate boolean Optional Activate the effect immediately on spawn Default: true.
dry_run boolean Optional Resolve the system without spawning Default: false.

niagara_system_inspect

Dump a NiagaraSystem asset's structure: emitter handles (name/enabled/sim-target), exposed USER parameters (name/type/is_data_interface), data interfaces, fixed-bounds flag, warmup time and effect type. The inspection-first paired read for the VFX authoring tools. Emitter-handle and exposed-parameter reflection is UNCERTAIN-API in 5.7 — anything unresolved is reported in warnings[] rather than guessed.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
system_path string Required Content path of the NiagaraSystem asset

niagara_systems

List/paginate NiagaraSystem assets (path + name) under a content root via the AssetRegistry — the entry read for VFX discovery. Named niagara_systems to avoid colliding with the dormant satellite-plugin C++ niagara_list command; adds prefix + limit/offset pagination.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
path_prefix string Optional Content root to search under, e.g. "/Game/VFX" Default: "/Game".
limit integer Optional Max systems to return Default: 50.
offset integer Optional Offset for pagination Default: 0.

niagara_validate

PLUMB-style read-only check of a NiagaraSystem: GPU emitters without fixed bounds, missing effect type, no emitters. Returns categorised violations with severity; ok:false only on errors. Emitter reflection is UNCERTAIN-API — gaps are reported as info-level violations rather than false positives. (autofix not implemented this wave — fixed:[] always.)

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
system_path string Required Content path of the NiagaraSystem to validate

Objects and reflection 6

object_exists

Existence probe: does an asset path, object path, or level-actor label resolve? Returns {exists, kind}. Cheap guard before a load/edit.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
target string Required Object/asset path or level-actor label to test for existence

object_get_property

Generic reflection read on any loadable UObject — replaces get_editor_property python_run pokes. Values are UE ExportText strings. PARAMS: `path` (object/asset path) + optional `names` — NOT widget_blueprint_path/widget_name; those belong to the ui_* tools. To reach a widget's slot, pass the slot's full object path as `path`.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
path string Required Object/asset path, e.g. /Game/Foo/MyAsset or a sub-object path
names any[] Optional Optional list of property names to read; omit to dump all editable (CPF_Edit) properties

object_inspect

Read the property tree of any live UObject by path (asset or object) or by level-actor label, filtered + paginated. The generic read-back primitive (actor_inspect is the richer level-actor variant). Differs from the legacy object_get_property (C++-backed, reads one CPF_Edit property by exact path, no actor-label resolution): use object_inspect to explore/discover an object's shape, object_get_property once you know the exact property path.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
target string Required Object path (e.g. "/Game/BP_Foo.BP_Foo_C") or a level-actor label
filter string Optional Case-insensitive substring filter on property names
limit integer Optional Max properties returned (pagination) Default: 80.
offset integer Optional Pagination offset Default: 0.

object_set_property

Generic reflection write on any loadable UObject (Modify + PostEditChange + MarkPackageDirty) — replaces set_editor_property python_run pokes. PARAMS: `path` (object/asset path) + `properties` (name to value map) — NOT widget_blueprint_path/widget_name/property; those belong to the ui_* tools. For textures prefer texture_set_settings; for material nodes prefer the material_* tools.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
path string Required Object/asset path
properties object (map) Required name to value map (numbers/strings/bools/arrays); set via reflection (HaybaReflection::SetProp)

reflect_class

Describe a UClass: python superclass chain (MRO) and CDO default-object attribute names, with values included for simple scalar types (str/int/float/bool) — so agents stop guessing class shapes before spawning/editing. (Class flags/interfaces need C++ reflection — not exposed to python.)

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
class_path string Required Class name (e.g. "StaticMeshComponent") or full class path

reflect_search_types

Fuzzy-search the UE python type system (classes/structs/enums exposed on the unreal module) by name substring. Turns "what's the class called?" into one call.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
query string Required Case-insensitive substring to match against type names in the unreal module
limit integer Optional Max matches returned Default: 30.

pcg_add_node

Add a node of a given PCG settings class to a graph. Returns node_index, settings_class, and node_label — node_label is now the friendly display title (e.g. "Shape : 3D Grid") when the HaybaPCGLibrary C++ helper is available, else it falls back to the settings-class name. For STABLE addressing pass either node_index or settings_class to pcg_wire/pcg_set_prop/pcg_remove_node (class-name and index addressing always work; friendly-title addressing depends on the node having an authored title). New nodes land at (0,0) — run pcg_layout afterward to arrange the graph. To remove a node use pcg_remove_node; to inspect its pins before wiring use pcg_list_pins.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
graph string Required PCG graph asset path
settings_class string Required PCG settings class name, e.g. "PCGSurfaceSamplerSettings" or "PCGSubdivideSettings"

pcg_cook_and_wait

Regenerate an actor's PCGComponent, block on the PCG graph settling (NOT world_tick), and return per-mesh ISM instance counts — all in one call. [cost=high] [effects=[mutates_scene,gpu_load,wait]] USE_WHEN: after editing a PCG graph, to regenerate an actor AND read back instance counts in ONE call — PCGComponent.generate is async, so a plain generate reads 0 instances in the same call. GROUND TRUTH is result.ism[] ({mesh,count} per ISM) — trust this over pcg_read_node_output (a possibly-stale inspection cache). result.freshness {changed,before,after} proves the counts are from THIS cook, not a prior run. idle.timedOut:["pcg"] is EXPECTED/BENIGN for PCGEx async chains and does NOT mean the cook failed (see idle_note); when result.ism is non-empty the cook succeeded regardless of the pcg idle timeout NOT_WHEN: you only want to read existing instances without regenerating — use pcg_inspect_instances

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
actor string Required Label or path of the actor owning the PCGComponent to cook
timeout_s integer Optional Hard timeout waiting for the PCG graph to settle Default: 120.

Struct properties accept a JSON object (coerced field-by-field, recursively) or a positional array (e.g. [x,y,z] for a Vector). pcg_wire

Wire one PCG node's output pin to another node's input pin (by node title or index, and pin label). Pin names are VALIDATED first: if from_pin/to_pin does not exist on the node, no wire is created and the result is {ok:false, error, valid_from_pins, valid_to_pins} — it never silently drops the edge. Use pcg_list_pins to discover exact labels. To cut an existing edge use pcg_disconnect.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
graph string Required PCG graph asset path

from_pin string Optional Source output pin label (default "Out") Default: "Out".
to_node string | integer Required Target node title or index. Use "Output" to wire into the graph's output node.
to_pin string Optional Target input pin label (default "In"). NOTE: the visible "Map" pin on PCGEx Staging is internally "CollectionSource" — introspect first if unsure. Default: "In".

read_node_output

STALE-READ WARNING: reads a possibly-STALE inspection CACHE, not live post-cook data. point_count can report 0 (or a prior run's numbers) while the cook actually produced real instances — do NOT treat point_count:0 here as ground truth. GROUND TRUTH for instance counts is `pcg_cook_and_wait` result.ism[] (with result.freshness.changed proving this cook). Returns zero counts if the graph has not been executed. FOLLOW-UP (C++): make this read live post-cook data or return an explicit {stale:true} flag.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
assetPath string Required UE object path to the PCGGraph asset
nodeId string Required Node id from the export_graph payload (e.g. 'node_003')

Physics 3

physics_add_impulse

Applies an impulse to a primitive component in the editor world and reports the resulting linear velocity. A component that is not simulating physics discards an impulse silently, so that case is REFUSED with a message naming the fix rather than answering applied:true — the old reply was true of the call and false of the world. Turn simulation on with physics_set_simulate first.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
actor_id string Required
impulse any[] Required [x,y,z]. Fewer than three numbers is rejected rather than zero-filled.
velocity_change boolean Optional true applies the vector as a velocity change, ignoring mass
component_name string Optional

physics_set_collision_profile

Assigns a named collision profile to one primitive component and READS IT BACK. An unrecognised name leaves the component on whatever it had, so a mismatch between requested_profile and profile is returned as an error naming the current setting rather than as a success. Names come from the project Collision settings, e.g. BlockAll, NoCollision, Pawn. This SETS a profile; to find out what is currently intersecting what, use scene_validate_physics.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
actor_id string Required
profile_name string Required A profile from Project Settings > Collision, e.g. BlockAll, OverlapAllDynamic, NoCollision
component_name string Optional Defaults to the root primitive component

physics_set_simulate

Turns rigid-body simulation on or off for one primitive component in the EDITOR world. The reply reads the flag back off the component rather than repeating the request, so a component that cannot simulate (no collision, no body instance) is visible as simulating:false with ok:true. Editor-world only: this is not how you drive physics during PIE.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
actor_id string Required Actor name or editor label in the current editor world
enabled boolean Required
component_name string Optional Which primitive component. Omitted means the root component, falling back to the first primitive component found.

plumb_validate

VERIFY PLACEMENT IS ACTUALLY CORRECT: runs the PLUMB constraint library over a set of instances and returns a directional Verdict — per-gate ok, signed value_m (how far off, and which way), and a FixVector telling you exactly how to move each instance to satisfy it. Catches grounding, clearance, alignment, spacing and interpenetration violations the viewport would reveal but you cannot. Hard fails set stopped_at; soft fails accumulate soft_cost. WHY: this is the quantified check that turns "looks placed" into "provably grounded and non-overlapping".

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
instances object[] Required Instances to validate (object id + optional asset/tags + transform)
constraint_ids string[] Optional Restrict to these library constraint ids; default = all enabled
write_overlay boolean Optional Also write per-instance results to .scratch/verdicts.json for the plan-mode viewport overlay
record_findings boolean Optional Record constraint failures as validator findings in the unified Validation surface (default true)

Python 1

python_run

Execute a Python script inside UE via PythonScriptPlugin. Universal escape hatch for invoking any UE command not otherwise exposed.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
script string Required Python source to execute. Runs in a FRESH namespace per call (__name__ == "__hayba_user__"): nothing is pre-imported, so `import unreal` explicitly, and no state survives from a previous python_run. Only print() output and stderr come back — assign nothing and you observe nothing.
allow_unsafe boolean Optional Deprecated compatibility field; accepted but always ineffective. Embedded python_run permanently refuses Tier 3 host filesystem, subprocess, and network access. Use typed brokered tools (#412/#415).
deadline_s number Optional Cooperative deadline in seconds (default 5, max 60). Above 5 requires an exclusive lease on the current world (lease_acquire mode:"exclusive"); otherwise the editor refuses it with HCR-TIME-002.
world_partition boolean Optional Set true when the script loads or unloads World Partition actors. The editor then skips its global undo transaction, which WP unloads corrupt (UTransBuffer non-zero active count, then a Landscape crash). Scripts using WorldPartitionEditorLoaderAdapter / load_actors / unload_actors are detected automatically.
transaction boolean Optional false = do not wrap this call in an editor undo transaction (no Ctrl+Z for it). Default true.
read_only boolean Optional Declare that the script only reads. The editor then treats it as a read for leases. Undeclared scripts conflict with every other owner's lease (X on global) under EnforcedForWrites.
resources string | object[] Optional Declare what the script writes (same forms as lease_acquire, e.g. "asset:/Game/Props/SM_Rock"). A declared script conflicts only with leases on those resources.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
asset_path string Required Content path of the LevelSequence
track_type "transform" | "float" | "visibility" | "camera_cuts" | "audio" | "event" Required Track type to add
binding_guid string Optional Binding GUID for a per-actor track; omit for a master track
dry_run boolean Optional Report the resolved track class without adding it Default: false.

seq_transform_keyframe

Keyframe location/rotation/scale on a possessed actor's transform track at a time (seconds), creating the track/section if absent. Closes the C++ gap where the dormant seq_add_keyframe is float-only. Channels resolved by name prefix (Location/Rotation/Scale) + axis suffix; keys authored in tick resolution.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
asset_path string Required Content path of the LevelSequence
binding_guid string Required Binding GUID of the possessed actor to keyframe
time_seconds number Required Time (seconds) at which to place the key
location number[] Optional World location [x,y,z]
rotation number[] Optional Rotation [roll,pitch,yaw] degrees
scale number[] Optional Scale [x,y,z]

seq_validate

PLUMB-style read-only check of a sequence: dangling bindings (no tracks), empty tracks (no sections), sections out of the playback range, missing/empty camera cut, zero-length playback. Returns categorised issues with severity; ok:false only on errors. (autofix not implemented this wave — fixed:[] always.)

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
asset_path string Required Content path of the LevelSequence to validate

hayba_sliver_get

Get the full spec (params + determinism + executor) of an installed sliver by id.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription

hayba_sliver_import

Not callable through hayba_invoke. Load its pack with hayba_pack_load first.

Install a sliver from a local file path or an http(s) URL into the user sliver library.

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
source string Required

hayba_sliver_list

Not callable through hayba_invoke. Load its pack with hayba_pack_load first.

List installed Slivers (deterministic abstractions). Optional category or namespace filter.

namespace string Optional

hayba_sliver_run

Not callable through hayba_invoke. Load its pack with hayba_pack_load first.

Execute a sliver with concrete parameter values. Returns outputs + declared side_effects + durationMs.
